THOUGHT: This is an older patient with a subacute (3-week) history of headache and progressive visual loss. Fundoscopic findings suggesting retinal vein engorgement/hemorrhages point toward a hyperviscosity-related retinopathy. Laboratory testing shows a monoclonal pentameric immunoglobulin on serum electrophoresis, which is characteristic of IgM. A monoclonal IgM-producing lymphoplasmacytic disorder in an older adult that commonly presents with hyperviscosity (headache, visual disturbances, retinal hemorrhages/venous dilation, possible mucosal bleeding or neurological symptoms) is Waldenström macroglobulinemia (IgM monoclonal gammopathy). Multiple myeloma is less likely given the IgM (not IgG/IgA), lack of anemia, hypercalcemia, renal failure, or lytic bone lesions. Therefore the most likely diagnosis is Waldenström macroglobulinemia causing hyperviscosity syndrome from an IgM monoclonal gammopathy.

DIAGNOSIS: Waldenström macroglobulinemia (IgM monoclonal gammopathy) with hyperviscosity syndrome
